key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual over days, often follows upper respiratory infection. LOCATION: Diffuse chest, trachea, bronchi. DURATION: 1-3 weeks, typically self-limiting. CHARACTER: Dry cough initially, becomes productive with yellow/green sputum. AGGRAVATING: Cold air, talking, laughing, lying flat. RELIEVING: Warm liquids, humid air, cough suppressants (limited). TIMING: Persistent throughout day, worse at night. SEVERITY: Mild to moderate (3-6/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Sore throat, nasal congestion, low-grade fever (rare), chest discomfort, fatigue. KEY POSITIVES: Productive cough, chest congestion, recent URI symptoms. KEY NEGATIVES: No high fever, no severe dyspnea, no chest pain.
